title: Standard Library Practice Exam
description: Practice collections, enum, math/random, and copy/deepcopy.

questions.explanation: Counter maps keys to counts, handy for tallies.

options: KeyError when accessing a missing key with a default factory
questions.explanation: Missing keys call the factory (e.g. list) to create a default value.

options: Named constants with a fixed set of values
questions.explanation: Enums make valid states explicit and readable.
randint is inclusive on both ends for integers.
math module functions often return floats.

questions.prompt: copy.copy makes a shallow copy of a collection.
questions.explanation: Nested objects may still be shared between original and shallow copy.

options: Nested mutable objects must be duplicated independently
questions.explanation: deepcopy recursively copies inner objects.
deque is optimized for queue-like operations.

options: One random element from the sequence
questions.explanation: choice selects a single item uniformly from a non-empty sequence.

questions.prompt: random.seed() can make random sequences reproducible for testing.
questions.explanation: Same seed yields the same pseudo-random sequence.

questions.prompt: After b = a on a list, mutating b affects a when:
options: You did not copy; both names refer to the same list
questions.explanation: Assignment shares references; use copy or slice to duplicate.

questions.prompt: Color.RED if Color is an Enum means:
options: A member of the Color enumeration
questions.explanation: Enum members compare by identity and have .name and .value.
floor rounds toward negative infinity.

options: The two most frequent items and their counts
questions.explanation: most_common helps find top frequencies quickly.

questions.prompt: The standard library ships with Python and does not require pip for those modules.
questions.explanation: collections, math, random, copy, enum are in the stdlib.

options: Copies outer list but inner lists may still be shared
questions.explanation: Inner objects are not recursively duplicated in a shallow copy.
shuffle reorders the existing list and returns None.
namedtuple improves readability for fixed-field records.

questions.prompt: When to prefer deepcopy over copy?
options: Nested mutables must not alias the original
questions.explanation: Use deepcopy when inner objects must be independent.

questions.prompt: Exploring help() on a stdlib module is a good way to discover useful tools.
questions.explanation: Python's batteries included philosophy means many tools are already there.
